overview:
UNIFIED PHASED BUILD PLAN — Voxeldust greenfield. ONE solo developer (with AI assist). The non-negotiable spine, drawn directly from all four subsystem designs (connection M0-M3, transfer M1-M6, identity Phase0-3, harness vertical-slice order): the deterministic test harness is the FIRST code; STUB shards (points in empty space, no terrain/physics) prove the ENTIRE transfer machinery — gateway one-connection multiplexing, authority directory with fencing tokens, durable saga, frozen ghosts, all 4 transition classes, full crash + chaos matrix, kill -9 resilience — BEFORE a single voxel exists. The user must watch two dots cross shard boundaries and survive kill -9 before terrain. Only then do terrain+meshing, physics, block-edits+persistence, ships, functional-blocks, and combat layer in, each gated by a harness regression suite the prior phases established.

Three cross-cutting invariants thread every phase and define every regression gate: (1) AUTHORITY-UNIQUE — exactly one Owner per entity at every committed tick, enforced by the directory CAS + Fence(u64) generation token, asserted by the ControlOracle from ground-truth directory state; (2) WIRE-TRUTH — every player-visible invariant (NO-VANISH, POSE-CONTINUITY, INPUT-CONSERVATION) is asserted against the BYTES the scripted client actually received after the FaultFabric mangled the link, never against a node's internal ECS state (the meta-test deliberately diverges ECS from wire and proves the WireMonitor fails); (3) SEAMLESS — the client holds exactly ONE QUIC connection for its whole session, never re-homes, never sees a shard; a transfer is a server-side route swap; FREEZE window is a tested sub-tick invariant.

The wire format and the three contract seams (Transfer Saga commands, Authority Directory query API, identity-ticket format) are FROZEN as shared-crate types with both-sided conformance tests BEFORE the gateway route-swap or resume logic is built — so correctness is never defined in terms of charters that don't exist yet. Every node type is lib+thin-bin (4-line main); bins depend on libs, never the reverse; production code touches time/rng/persistence/transport ONLY through injected ShardIo traits (enforced by scoped clippy disallowed_methods/disallowed_types, not a bespoke grep). The reference repo at branch ecs-system is SPEC ONLY: port proven PURE functions with their tests (compute_soi_radius, system_soi_radius kept distinct, planet_rotation freefall formula, Kepler solve, greedy meshing adapter) — re-derive nothing by hand-matching formulas across binaries.

Client track runs in PARALLEL: a scripted/headless client drives the harness from Phase 0; a minimal wgpu render window appears once snapshots flow (Phase 1.5/2); the real interactive client replaces scripted clients incrementally and is feature-complete-enough to fly a ship across a boundary by the ship phase. No client-side prediction anywhere — pure server-authoritative interpolation on a 100-150ms buffer evaluating time-parameterized reference-frame functions at render time.

Riskiest phases flagged with de-risking spikes up front: P0a (the sync-step_tick / async-QUIC bridge tracer bullet — the threading model everything depends on), P3 (QUIC datagram multiplexing latency + MTU-clamp under a 4MB BULK burst on the k3d VXLAN overlay), P6/P7 (Rapier world snapshot/restore + cross-binary float determinism boundary), P10 (dual-frame ship interior physics). Each is preceded by a named spike that must pass before the phase is trusted.
workspace_layout:
## Workspace layout — start at ~7 crates, grow on real pressure (NOT 12 up front)

The greenfield workspace is genuinely empty (the old-repo copy in the worktree is reference only). Every node type is **lib + thin 4-line bin**. Production I/O (quinn/tokio/redb/SystemTime/rand) is reachable ONLY behind injected traits; scoped `clippy.toml` `disallowed-methods`/`disallowed-types` in `sim`/`node` forbids direct `SystemTime::now`, `Instant::now`, `thread_rng`, and default-`RandomState` `HashMap`.

### Phase-0 crates (built first, in this order)
- **`core`** (lib) — pure, shard-agnostic domain types and PURE functions. EntityId(u128), SessionId(u128), TransferId(u128), Fence(u64), TickId, EpochId. Seed-derived world params (no magic numbers). Ported-with-tests reference functions live here: `geometry::planet_soi` (Hill sphere, mass ratio) and `geometry::system_soi` (BASE + luminosity*scale) kept as **separately named, doc-commented, tested** functions with a CI test asserting they differ by the expected order of magnitude. Closed-form celestial math (Kepler solve, mean-anomaly) marked Category-A (analytic, bit-deterministic). Depends on: glam, noise(pinned), brahe(pinned). NO quinn/redb/rapier/tokio.
- **`wire`** (lib) — THE frozen wire contract. The four typed channel families as closed enums (ControlMsg, InputDatagram, BulkMsg, EventMsg, SnapshotDatagram), the StreamFrame/datagram framing, postcard serialization (codec_flags bit reserved for future bitcode, always 0 in v1), proto-version negotiation types. Plus the three first-class SEAM contracts: `TransferControl` saga command/ack enum, Directory query/CAS API, `SessionTicket`/`ResumeTicket` shapes. Both-sided conformance tests live against this crate. Depends on: core, postcard, serde.
- **`sim`** (lib) — pure ECS world + systems + the saga state machine and authority FSM as pure `fn step(State,Event)->(State,Vec<Action>)`, AND the `sim::io` MODULE defining the injected traits: `Transport` (enqueue-only `send -> Result<(),QueueFull>`, `drain_inbound -> Vec<Inbound>` incl. NodeUnreachable/ProvisionResult), `Clock` (logical now/tick/universe_epoch), `Store` (WAL-buffer put, no fsync; take_pending; durable_through), `DetRng`, `Provisioner`. `sim::io::mem` provides the in-memory test impls (MeshFabric handle, VirtualClock, MemStore). Depends on: core, wire, bevy_ecs (SingleThreaded executor). NO quinn/redb/tokio.
- **`node`** (lib) — `build_app(NodeKind, NodeConfig, IO) -> ShardNode<IO>` for ALL node kinds (Gateway, Orchestrator, StubShard, and later SystemShard/PlanetShard/ShipShard) behind a NodeKind param. `step_tick() -> TickReport` is THE deterministic unit of progress; `run_forever()` is the prod loop. Bins are 4-line wrappers building ProdIo and calling build_app. Depends on: sim, wire, core.
- **`harness`** (lib + tests) — `Topology` (BTreeMap of nodes, deterministic iteration), `FaultFabric` (at-least-once redelivery, drop/dup/reorder/delay/partition/send-reject/crash-with CrashWhen{PreInject,PostInject,PostStep}/resurrect), `VirtualClock`, `StaggerPlan` (per-node tick offset), `ScriptedClient` + `ClientScript` trait, `ControlOracle` (ground-truth: directory + saga records only), `WireMonitor` (decodes ONLY fabric-delivered bytes), `ChaosRunner(seed)` with twice-in-separate-processes byte-identical replay gate. Depends on: node, sim::io::mem, wire.
- **`tests`** (test crate) — in-process scenario suites. Every later phase ADDS scenarios here; nothing is deleted.

### Bins (thin wrappers, added as phases need them)
- **`gateway`** (bin) — owns the ONE client QUIC connection; multiplexes CONTROL bidi + INPUT/SNAPSHOT datagrams + per-sub BULK/EVENTS uni streams; validates ticket + lease_epoch/gateway_gen fence on every frame; lock-free ArcSwap route table on the hot path.
- **`orchestrator`** (bin) — hosts the Authority Directory (redb, fenced, CAS), the Transfer Coordinator (per-key-serialized saga, redb WAL group-commit), the durable monotonic UniverseClock (write-ahead tick ceiling), the Ephemeris Authority, and a read-only admin HTTP endpoint (dump saga by correlation_id, directory ownership+fence, lease health) + Prometheus metrics.
- **`auth`** (bin) — SEPARATE small service: Argon2id verify off the orchestrator's saga-timer threads.
- **`shard`** (bin) — one binary, `ShardKind` param; `fn main(){ node::run(NodeKind::from(cfg), cfg, ProdIo::bind(cfg)) }`. Stub in early phases; gains terrain/physics/blocks/ships in later phases behind the SAME build_app seam.
- **`client`** (bin) — wgpu+winit+egui interactive client; net module is ~one task (read CONTROL+per-sub streams+SNAPSHOT datagrams, demux by sub_id into render layers, write INPUT datagrams at 20Hz, emit CUT_MARKER on request). No ConnectionMode/observer/promotion logic.

### GROW LATER (only when a real second impl or compile pain forces the split)
- **`io-prod`** — split out of `sim::io` when the quinn/tokio/redb impls exist (a SECOND impl is what justifies the seam). Carries `#![allow(clippy::disallowed_methods)]`.
- **`tests-process`** — real-binary localhost tier (real QUIC handshakes, redb files, identity headers) added once io-prod exists.
- **`vd-fence` / `vd-time` / `vd-store` / `vd-saga`** — the identity_persistence design names these as separate crates; pragmatically they begin life as MODULES inside `core`/`sim`/`node` and are extracted to crates only if compile-time or a second consumer demands it. The fencing primitive (Fence/lease_epoch/gateway_gen) and the durable clock are the load-bearing pieces and must exist as types from Phase 0 regardless of crate boundary.

Dependency rule (enforced): bins -> node -> sim -> wire -> core. harness -> node + sim::io::mem. io-prod -> sim (implements its traits). Nothing depends on a bin. core depends on no other workspace crate.
spikes: SPIKE-0a (BLOCKING, before P0 proper): Sync-step_tick / async-QUIC bridge tracer bullet. Build a stub node + ProdIo reader/writer tokio tasks bridging crossbeam queues to a synchronous step_tick over in-memory queue snapshots, no gameplay. Prove: the sim thread never .awaits wall time; Transport::send is enqueue-only and returns Err(QueueFull) under backpressure; a hard send failure re-enters as Inbound::NodeUnreachable next tick. This is the threading model EVERYTHING depends on; if it doesn't hold, the whole determinism story collapses. Exit: tracer bullet passes a 1000-tick virtual-clock test AND a real-quinn-loopback smoke test with identical logical output.

SPIKE-3a (BLOCKING, before P3 transfer-over-real-QUIC trust): QUIC datagram multiplexing under load on the k3d overlay. Real-quinn loopback + a lossy/MTU-clamped UDP shim. Measure: SNAPSHOT+INPUT datagram delivery ratio while a 4MB BULK fresh-subscribe burst fills the congestion window; assert conn.max_datagram_size() >= datagram_budget after the k3d VXLAN (~50B) clamp; assert BULK application-pacing (bulk_budget_bytes_per_rtt from live quinn RTT) keeps datagram delivery >= target; assert SendDatagramError::TooLarge surfaces LOUD on a metric, never silent. Exit: documented delivery-ratio curve + a CI assertion that fails if pacing regresses. De-risks the connection-plane's single biggest unproven claim.

SPIKE-6a (BLOCKING, before P6 physics authority on real binaries): Rapier3d world snapshot/restore + cross-binary float determinism boundary. Build the Category-A vs Category-C boundary harness: compile `core` into a tiny standalone binary, run on two target-cpu/profile builds, assert bitwise-equal transfer_frame outputs on seed+tick fixtures (FMA contraction forbidden in frames.rs; glam/brahe pinned identical). Separately prove Rapier state is checkpoint-carried, NEVER re-simulated on a different host: snapshot a rapier world to redb, drop it, re-open, restore, assert the restored kinematic state matches and that free-fall re-advance uses the closed-form ballistic solve (not a rapier step). Exit: the determinism CI gate is green and the snapshot/restore round-trips within tolerance.

SPIKE-10a (before P10 ship interior physics): Dual-frame ship-interior spike. Prove a player walked-inside a ship rigid body that is itself a rapier body in a host frame: two rapier worlds (interior private world owned by ship-shard + exterior hull body in host), KCC against the interior floor while the hull accelerates (Newtonian), and the ReferenceFrameDef(rigid parent transform) lets the client composite interior pose through hull pose at one render tick with no jitter. Exit: a scripted client walks a corridor while the ship boosts and the WireMonitor POSE-CONTINUITY (with stagger) passes.

SPIKE-2a (small, before P2 saga route-swap): Lock-free hot-path proof. Microbenchmark the gateway 20Hz input route decision reading route via ArcSwap::load + last_input_seq via AtomicU64, with a concurrent control-path publishing a new RouteSnapshot via atomic store. Assert no torn read (authority+seq_cut in ONE Arc), no async lock held across an awaited send, p99 route decision < 50us. De-risks the Attack-2.4 lock-discipline claim cheaply.

phases.name: P0 — Foundation: harness skeleton, frozen wire, contract seams, fencing primitive
phases.deliverables: Empty cargo workspace with core/wire/sim/node/harness/tests crates. SPIKE-0a tracer bullet landed (sync step_tick over crossbeam bridge). The FROZEN wire contract in `wire`: ControlMsg/InputDatagram/BulkMsg/EventMsg/SnapshotDatagram enums, StreamFrame framing, postcard codec (bit reserved for bitcode), proto-version negotiation. The three SEAM contracts as shared types with both-sided conformance tests: TransferControl saga command/ack enum, Directory query+CAS API, SessionTicket/ResumeTicket shapes. The linearizability core: Fence(u64), OwnerRecord, lease_epoch, gateway_gen, CAS semantics, self-fence-before-grant rules — as pure types + a pure FSM. sim::io traits + sim::io::mem impls (VirtualClock, MemStore WAL-buffer-no-fsync, MeshFabric, DetRng, InProcProvisioner with persist-intent-before-spawn + controllable async gap). Topology + FaultFabric (at-least-once redelivery, CrashWhen 3-phase, drop/dup/reorder/delay/partition/send-reject) + ControlOracle + WireMonitor + ChaosRunner with twice-in-separate-processes replay gate. clippy.toml disallowed-methods/types. Durable monotonic UniverseClock (write-ahead tick ceiling, backward-slew forbidden). Ported PURE reference functions WITH their tests: planet_soi, system_soi (distinct), planet_rotation freefall formula, Kepler solve, greedy-meshing adapter signature (math only, not wired). HMAC SessionTicket + static cluster-PSK mTLS config types (day-1 trust). Orchestrator admin HTTP endpoint shell + Prometheus metric names.
phases.definition_of_done: Workspace compiles green. The tracer bullet passes a 1000-tick virtual-clock test AND a real-quinn-loopback smoke test producing identical logical output. The saga FSM + authority FSM pass proptest over random event sequences (no illegal state, guaranteed termination). The three seam conformance suites pass both-sided (gateway-side stub + saga-side stub). ChaosRunner replays a seed twice in separate processes with byte-identical logical traces. The meta-test that deliberately diverges a node's ECS state from its delivered snapshots PROVES the WireMonitor fails (the harness can see the connect_tx bug class). UniverseClock backward-slew is rejected by test. clippy passes with the disallowed-methods/types rules. Determinism CI gate skeleton exists (even if no transfer yet).
phases.demo: Headless: `cargo test` runs the full Phase-0 suite in milliseconds (12000 virtual ticks, zero real sleep). `curl` the orchestrator admin endpoint and get an empty-but-shaped directory/saga dump. A reproducibility demo: same CHAOS_SEED twice -> identical trace. Nothing visible on screen yet — this phase's product is a TRUSTWORTHY FEEDBACK LOOP, not pixels.
phases.harness_scenarios: Foundation scenarios (all later phases extend these, none are deleted): saga-FSM proptest; authority-FSM proptest; seam conformance (Transfer/Directory/Ticket); ChaosRunner reproducibility gate; the WireMonitor meta-divergence test; UniverseClock monotonicity test; Fence CAS mutual-exclusion test (COMMIT-vs-ABORT loser no-ops).
phases.risks: HIGHEST-RISK PHASE despite no gameplay — if the step_tick/async-bridge model (SPIKE-0a) or the wire/seam freeze is wrong, everything downstream inherits the flaw. Mitigation: SPIKE-0a is BLOCKING; freeze the wire + 3 seams with conformance tests before any consumer is built. Risk of over-engineering 12 crates up front — mitigated by starting at 6 and the GROW-LATER rule. Risk of the determinism story being aspirational — mitigated by the twice-in-separate-processes gate and the meta-divergence test being written NOW.

phases.name: P1 — STUB shards: single-shard connect+walk, ONE connection, no transfer
phases.deliverables: node::build_app for NodeKind::Gateway, Orchestrator, StubShard. A StubShard simulates entities as POINTS in empty space (no terrain, no physics, no rapier — pose is a kinematic integrator or scripted path). Gateway M0 walking skeleton: forwards exactly ONE subscription, ONE authority, snapshots verbatim with sub_id=0, input datagrams verbatim, dev-static SessionTicket (HMAC), plaintext dev cert. In-memory Authority Directory (single owner, fenced). ScriptedClient holds exactly ONE logical connection to a gateway NodeId and asserts its route target never changes. The DurableUniverseClock drives ticks. ConnectionPlane M0 + identity Phase-0 (HMAC ticket validated at gateway, session_id is the cross-shard principal, shards never see the ticket).
phases.definition_of_done: A scripted client logs in (HMAC ticket), subscribes to one stub shard, sends 20Hz input datagrams, and receives 20Hz snapshot datagrams of its own moving point + other clients' points on the same shard. AUTHORITY-UNIQUE holds (exactly one Owner). INPUT-CONSERVATION holds (every input appears in exactly one applied-log or a reasoned discard-log). The client's connection target NodeId is asserted constant. Works in-process (VirtualClock) AND as real binaries on localhost QUIC (gateway+orchestrator+one stub shard) with the SAME logical assertions.
phases.demo: Two scripted dots move around one stub shard, visible via a logged/JSON snapshot dump OR an early debug 2D plot. On real binaries: `dev-cluster.sh` brings up orchestrator+gateway+one stub shard; a headless client connects and walks; admin endpoint shows one session, one owner. This is the first end-to-end 'a player exists in the world' moment.
phases.harness_scenarios: Single-shard walk scenario (in-process + real-binary tiers). INPUT-CONSERVATION under input-datagram drop (skip-a-tick-apply-next-fresh, no wedge). Ticket-validation rejection tests (bad HMAC, wrong epoch, expired). Connection-target-constant assertion. Adds the real-binary `tests-process` tier (io-prod split happens here — the second Transport impl forces the seam).
phases.risks: Temptation to add features before transfer works — the user's #1 failure mode. Mitigation: STUB shards have NO terrain/physics by design; this phase is deliberately boring. Real-QUIC vs in-memory semantic drift — mitigated by running identical logical assertions on both tiers.

phases.name: P1.5 — Client render bring-up (PARALLEL track start)
phases.deliverables: Minimal wgpu+winit+egui window. The client net module as ~one task: read CONTROL stream + SNAPSHOT datagrams, demux by sub_id into render layers, interpolate on a 100-150ms buffer, evaluate ReferenceFrameDef functions at render time, write INPUT datagrams at 20Hz, emit CUT_MARKER on request. Renders entities as simple billboards/cubes-as-points (no meshes yet). NO ConnectionMode/observer/promotion logic (that whole machinery is deleted by design). egui debug overlay: current sub_ids, authoritative sub per player, frame_ids, interp buffer depth.
phases.definition_of_done: A human opens the client window, sees their own dot and other dots moving on one stub shard, and can drive their dot with WASD+mouse (input datagrams). Interpolation is smooth at 100-150ms buffer with no prediction. The debug overlay shows exactly one authoritative sub for the local player.
phases.demo: First HUMAN-PLAYABLE moment: open the window, walk a dot around empty space, watch another scripted dot move. Replaces the old rebuild-k3d-and-fly-and-grep loop with a real window — but the SOURCE OF TRUTH for tests remains the WireMonitor, not the human.
phases.harness_scenarios: No new server-side scenarios; the client is validated against the same delivered-bytes the WireMonitor checks. Adds a client-side replay test: feed recorded delivered-snapshot bytes, assert deterministic render-layer composition.
phases.risks: Client work can balloon and distract from transfer hardening. Mitigation: keep it deliberately minimal (points, not meshes); the real client grows incrementally alongside server phases, it does NOT gate them. Scripted clients remain the primary test driver through P5.

phases.name: P2 — Multi-sub interest + the Transfer Saga: ONE transition class, frozen ghosts, ordered Demote-before-Promote
phases.deliverables: ConnectionPlane M1+M2 + Transfer Milestone-1. InterestSet diffs from the authoritative shard -> gateway -> monotonic never-reused sub_ids -> per-sub BULK/EVENTS uni streams -> hysteresis (enter_radius>exit_radius) + min subscription dwell + (stub) chunk cache. Spawn Resolver (stateless, computes initial interest from checkpoint pos) for bootstrap. The Transfer Coordinator drives ONE transition class end-to-end (pick SoiEntry or BoardShip — a stub-shard-to-stub-shard crossing): PrepareSubscribe(frozen-ghost passive mirror, NO independent physics) -> RequestCut -> client emits in-band CUT_MARKER token (triple-sent + CONTROL-confirmed) -> FreezeSource (route.cut atomic store, seq<=marker->source, seq>marker->dest buffer) -> ORDERED FENCE_DEMOTE (directory CAS version+1/lease_epoch+1, wait source DemoteAck) -> CommitAuthority (single atomic route store, gateway drops old-lease_epoch frames) -> ThawSource compensator + AbortTransfer on any pre-commit failure -> ReleaseSubscribe. Per-EntityId saga serialization lock. SPIKE-2a lock-free hot-path proof landed. Velocity-scaled overlap band (segment-vs-shell crossing, no tunneling). Gateway lease_epoch fence on every frame. Source authority RETAINED until dest Committed (B2 — never warp into nothing).
phases.definition_of_done: A scripted dot crosses ONE stub-shard boundary seamlessly: its single connection target NodeId never changes; AUTHORITY-UNIQUE holds at EVERY committed tick (len==1 exactly — catches both split-brain and zero-owner); POSE-CONTINUITY holds at the A->B owner flip (||Δpos|| < ε, ε derived from max_velocity*dt*(1+stagger)); NO-VANISH holds (frozen ghost exists on dest BEFORE commit, no visibility pop); INPUT-CONSERVATION holds across the cut (seq<=marker on source, seq>marker on dest, exactly once with dedup). The FREEZE window is a tested sub-tick invariant. ABORT-before-commit returns the dot to a live source with no stranded state. All under VirtualClock AND staggered-stepping (tick-skew exercised in the fast tier).
phases.demo: Two dots cross a shard boundary seamlessly in the client window — the human sees no hitch, no reconnect, no pop. The debug overlay shows the authoritative sub flipping while the connection stays put. The admin endpoint shows the saga timeline by correlation_id (PREPARE->FREEZE->FENCE_DEMOTE->COMMIT->RELEASE). THIS IS THE FIRST PROOF OF THE CORE THESIS.
phases.harness_scenarios: Seamless single-class transfer (happy path). ABORT-on-spatial-precondition-fail (typed TransferRejected). ThawSource-after-Freeze compensation. CUT_MARKER triple-send loss tolerance + CONTROL confirmation. Hysteresis ping-pong suppression (sustained-inward N_entry ticks + min-dwell cooldown; transfer_pingpong metric). sub_id never-reused + (sub_id,frame_id) stale-datagram drop. Frozen-ghost-is-passive-mirror (no second simulation => no visibility fork; A1 single-authoritative-sub). Staggered-stepping cross-shard POSE-CONTINUITY. These become PERMANENT GATES: no later phase may regress any of them.
phases.risks: The single most important phase to get right and the densest. The ordered Demote-before-Promote adds one RTT — accepted trade-off (entity is Frozen+interpolated across it). Risk that the lock-free hot path has a torn read — mitigated by SPIKE-2a and single-Arc RouteSnapshot. Risk of the cut racing a cross-stream message — structurally prevented by the in-band CUT_MARKER token on the ordered input stream.

phases.name: P3 — All 4 transition classes + the full crash & chaos matrix on stub shards
phases.deliverables: Transfer Milestone-2/3 + ConnectionPlane M3 + the remaining transition classes as typed payloads (ShipToSurface/SurfaceToShip, ShipToEva/EvaToShip, PlanetToSpace/SpaceToPlanet — all still on STUB shards, points in empty space). Durability: redb Authority Directory + group-commit saga WAL (separate redb files for saga vs directory); per-shard transfer-leg WAL with write-ahead BEFORE any world-mutating effect; idempotent effects keyed (TransferId,version) with correlation-id single-use-terminal tombstones (dup-PREPARE-after-ABORT is a no-op). Durable seq-range ownership interval map per txn in the directory (reconnect reloads ownership from directory, NEVER from client ticket). ResumeTicket (single-use nonce + session_gen fence + Ed25519/HMAC re-validate; cursor from durable checkpoint not ticket). Directory-mediated gateway adoption (gateway_gen CAS, old gateway self-fences). FENCE-THEN-FORCE bounded resolution (fence first via gateway lease_epoch drop, distinguish crash-vs-slow by lease/heartbeat, bounded+acknowledged InputGap). mTLS (static cluster PSK day-1). SPIKE-3a datagram-multiplexing-under-load gate landed. The full crash-recovery matrix: saga-phase × victim{source,dest,orchestrator,gateway} × CrashWhen{PreInject,PostInject,PostStep}, built last as one hand-written cell then macro-generated once the saga API is stable.
phases.definition_of_done: All 4 transition classes pass the P2 gate suite on stub shards. kill -9 of source, dest, gateway, or orchestrator at ANY saga phase/CrashWhen leaves the system at exactly one Owner, no stranded player, saga reaches COMMITTED or ABORTED. Resurrect-from-stale-checkpoint is FENCED OUT (the DURABILITY test resurrects a pre-COMMIT checkpoint, asserts the harness FAILS first to prove it can see the bug, then asserts the fence prevents it). Gateway crash -> client reconnects to the gateway VIP, re-presents ticket, re-binds to the existing session (reconnect-to-identity, NOT re-home-to-shard). ChaosRunner with bounded-healing partitions passes LIVENESS; permanent-partition passes NO-UNILATERAL-COMMIT (SAFETY). SPIKE-3a delivery-ratio gate green on the k3d overlay.
phases.demo: THE HEADLINE DEMO: two dots crossing shard boundaries (all 4 classes) while the operator runs `kill -9` on shards mid-transfer in a loop — the dots keep moving, never wedge, never duplicate, never vanish. `dev-cluster.sh` chaos mode + a `curl` of the admin endpoint shows every saga driving to a terminal state. This is the user's explicit gate: kill -9 resilience BEFORE any voxel exists.
phases.harness_scenarios: Full crash-recovery matrix (saga-phase × victim × CrashWhen). Resume nonce single-use + replay rejection. gateway_gen split-brain adoption fence. Durable seq-range interval map (replay-on-wrong-shard rejected). FENCE-THEN-FORCE crash-vs-slow + bounded InputGap. Chaos: bounded-partition LIVENESS + permanent-partition NO-UNILATERAL-COMMIT. Datagram-under-4MB-BULK-burst delivery ratio (real-quinn tier). Group-commit fsync p99 under 'everyone lands at once' load. ALL become permanent gates.
phases.risks: The chaos/crash matrix can bit-rot if built too early — mitigated by Tier-1 first (happy + FENCE-THEN-FORCE + spatial abort), Tier-2 (crash WAL re-drive) at this milestone, Tier-3 (orchestrator/gateway) initially ABORT-to-source (simpler, equally safe). SPIKE-3a is BLOCKING for trusting real-QUIC transfer. fsync convoy under load is real — mitigated by group-commit + lease-renewals-off-redb + measuring p99 before trusting the 1-2s timeouts.

phases.name: P4 — Terrain generation + meshing (from-scratch reimpl, old repo as SPEC)
phases.deliverables: Spherical voxel planet terrain: deterministic-from-seed (no chunk streaming, no networked terrain — only the seed crosses the wire). RE-DERIVE from spec (port the math, rewrite the code): PlanetParams::from_seed (radius 100k-200k blocks, gravity, rotation period via t_freefall=√(R³/GM)×calibrated multiplier), biome/geology noise stacks (pinned `noise`), the binary-greedy-meshing adapter on 62^3 chunks. RE-DESIGN (do NOT port the old structure): the chunk storage/palette/delta layout (Category-A analytic base + delta overlay), the shard-agnostic block registry. Terrain is Category-A (analytic, bit-deterministic), reconstructable on any host from (seed, chunk address) with ZERO networking. Client-side mesher mirrors the server's chunk math. Planet shards stop being stubs: they generate terrain but entities are STILL kinematic points (physics is P5).
phases.definition_of_done: Same seed produces byte-identical terrain on server and client and across two target-cpu builds (determinism CI gate extended to terrain). A planet shard generates a spherical voxel world; the client renders greedy-meshed chunks around the player. The chunk math is shard-agnostic (same code path a ship-interior realm will use). CRITICAL: ALL P2/P3 transfer gates still pass — terrain did not regress any transfer scenario (the harness re-runs the full crash+chaos matrix with terrain-bearing shards, entities still points).
phases.demo: Open the client and fly/walk over a procedurally generated spherical planet with real greedy-meshed voxel terrain — and STILL cross a planet<->space boundary seamlessly with kill -9 resilience. First time the world looks like a world.
phases.harness_scenarios: Terrain determinism (server==client==cross-binary). Chunk-mesh round-trip. MUST-NOT-REGRESS gate: the entire P2/P3 transfer+crash+chaos suite re-run with terrain-generating shards. A new 'transfer-near-terrain' scenario: a point crosses a boundary while both shards are generating terrain (terrain CPU load must not blow saga timeouts).
phases.risks: Terrain is a large surface that can swallow weeks. Mitigation: it's Category-A and networking-free, so it CANNOT corrupt the transfer machinery — it's structurally isolated. Risk of importing the old code's structure wholesale — mitigated by the re-derive-math/re-design-structure split. noise/glam version pins must match across binaries or determinism breaks.

phases.name: P5 — Physics: Rapier per shard, KCC, spherical gravity (players physically collide)
phases.deliverables: Rapier3d per shard (server-authoritative). Spherical gravity field (toward planet center, magnitude seed-derived per PlanetParams). Kinematic Character Controller (re-derive from old kcc_sys/controller/locomotion as SPEC): walk/run/jump against terrain colliders, stance. PLAYERS PHYSICALLY COLLIDE (binding requirement — capsule-vs-capsule). Category-C boundary enforced: rapier state is checkpoint-carried, NEVER re-simulated on a different host; every physics->control boundary QUANTIZED to integer grids (sector-edge, SOI, land/launch thresholds) so control flow never branches on raw f64. SPIKE-6a (rapier snapshot/restore + cross-binary determinism) landed. Frozen ghosts gain kinematic colliders (collide, never integrate). Transfer FREEZE/handoff carries exact pose+velocity+source_frozen_at_tick; dest re-evaluates forward (analytic for ballistic, never re-step rapier).
phases.definition_of_done: Players walk on the spherical surface under real gravity, collide with terrain and with each other, and a transfer carries exact rapier pose+velocity with POSE-CONTINUITY < ε at the flip (now with real physics, not a kinematic point). Rapier snapshot->redb->restore round-trips within tolerance. The determinism CI gate is green (control plane exact, physics within tolerance, physics_determinism a soft warn-only diagnostic run as two processes). MUST-NOT-REGRESS: full transfer+crash+chaos matrix passes with REAL physics entities, under staggered stepping.
phases.demo: Two human players walk around a spherical planet, bump into each other (real collision), jump, and walk across a sector-seam boundary into a neighbor shard's authority seamlessly — with the operator still able to kill -9 a shard mid-walk-across-boundary.
phases.harness_scenarios: KCC behavioral tests (walk/jump/collide on sphere). Player-vs-player collision. Quantized physics->control boundary replay determinism. Rapier snapshot/restore round-trip. Transfer-with-real-rapier-state POSE-CONTINUITY (incl. free-fall handoff: FREEZE forbidden unless analytic ballistic state checkpointed). Two-real-shards integration harness with packet loss on the ghost datagram path (where stutter bugs live and unit tests can't see them). Full matrix re-run with physics.
phases.risks: HIGH RISK — Rapier determinism and snapshot/restore are the second-biggest unproven area. Mitigation: SPIKE-6a BLOCKING; Category-A/C boundary makes rapier state checkpoint-only (never recomputed cross-host); quantization makes control-plane replay independent of float jitter. Risk of physics blowing the 50ms tick — mitigated by the off-tick persistence design and per-shard rapier worlds.

phases.name: P6 — Block edits + per-realm durable delta persistence
phases.deliverables: Server-authoritative block place/break as RELIABLE discrete actions (BULK[sub] C->G action frames or CONTROL with their own seq+ack — a lost block-edit is retried; movement stays latest-wins datagrams). Per-realm redb block store owned by EXACTLY ONE shard (directory RealmRef owner; edits from ghost/overlap regions FORWARDED to the realm owner, never written locally — single-writer redb safety). block_wal (append-only, 5-byte dedup-to-final edits, sorted-on-drain for determinism) + chunk_snapshot compaction via the three-step durable WAL-checkpoint discipline (write snapshot+fsync -> record durable LSN+fsync -> prune strictly <= LSN; recovery tolerates older WAL, idempotent last-writer-wins). DBs keyed by RealmId (not shard_id) on a persistent volume so re-sharding keeps edits. Edits networked as deltas only (the binding 'no chunk streaming' rule). Client applies edit deltas to its local meshed chunks. dev-cluster.sh atomic wipe-all-stores-together; every record tagged universe_epoch_id + epoch_schema_version (mismatch -> discard/abort, fail-safe).
phases.definition_of_done: A player breaks/places blocks; edits persist across shard kill -9 + restart (RealmId-keyed redb, WAL replay, compaction checkpoint never loses edits even crashing between steps). Edits are deltas on the wire (terrain itself never streamed). A re-sharded planet keeps its edits. MUST-NOT-REGRESS: full transfer+crash+chaos matrix + terrain + physics all still pass; a new scenario edits blocks DURING a transfer and asserts edits land exactly once on the realm owner.
phases.demo: A player digs a tunnel and builds a structure on the planet; kill -9 the planet shard; it restarts and the tunnel+structure are exactly as left. Another player on a neighboring shard sees the edits via forwarded deltas.
phases.harness_scenarios: Block-edit durability across crash (WAL replay + compaction-checkpoint crash-between-steps loses nothing). Edit-during-transfer exactly-once on realm owner. Edit-from-ghost-region forwarded-not-local-write. Deterministic WAL byte output (sorted drain). Epoch-mismatch fail-safe discard. Full matrix re-run with block edits.
phases.risks: Compaction prune-race is a classic lost-data bug — mitigated by the three-step durable checkpoint + idempotent replay. Multi-writer redb on one realm is a fatal-adjacent trap — mitigated by single-owner-forwarded-edits. Write amplification — mitigated by off-tick batched WAL writer (~1 fsync/250ms).

phases.name: P7 — Player checkpoints + full identity/persistence durability (MMO-grade)
phases.deliverables: Tiered player checkpoints: hot tier (pose/health) every 20 ticks coalesced into one redb txn/s (1 fsync/s for all players on a shard); warm tier (inventory/stance) write-on-change debounced ~5s. PlayerCheckpoint carries FrameRef + durable freeze marker. Session/identity hardening: key rotation (renewal mints fresh ticket on current key, absolute lifetime cap drains old keys), revocation set + session_validity_epoch (ban/logout/credential-change takes effect mid-session), epoch-rollover re-mint, conn_binding replay rejection, Argon2id in the SEPARATE auth service off the saga-timer threads. Reconnect-without-game-state-replay (fresh snapshot + only the bulk the client lacks, via the chunk cache keyed by edit_epoch). Orchestrator persisted universe epoch + write-ahead tick ceiling fully wired. Admin endpoint + Prometheus fully populated (saga_stuck_count, abort_rate, forced_commit_total, clock_skew_ms, orchestrator_write_txn_latency, ghost_staleness_seconds).
phases.definition_of_done: A player checkpoints periodically; on full-cluster restart (kill -9 everything), every player resumes at their last checkpoint with correct pose/inventory/health, exactly one Owner, no stuck saga, all block-edit deltas present. Revoked sessions are hard-invalidated mid-session before natural expiry. The universe epoch never resets (monotonic clock survives restart). 2am-debuggability: a stuck saga is diagnosable from one `curl`, not a grep loop. MUST-NOT-REGRESS: entire prior suite passes.
phases.demo: kill -9 the ENTIRE cluster (all shards + gateway + orchestrator) and bring it back; players resume exactly where they were — pose, dug tunnels, inventory — with no re-login game-state replay. `curl` the admin endpoint to watch sagas and leases recover. This is the 'MMO-grade durability from day one' proof.
phases.harness_scenarios: Full-cluster crash -> resume-from-checkpoint (exactly-one-owner, no stuck saga, edits present). Tiered-checkpoint cadence (write amplification within budget). Session revocation mid-session. Key rotation drains old keys. Epoch-rollover re-mint. Reconnect-without-replay (chunk cache hit). Orchestrator-crash lease-freeze (no reassignment storm). Full matrix re-run.
phases.risks: Single-orchestrator SPOF is an accepted, documented trade-off at this scale (fast-restart SLO <2s, lease-freeze-on-unreachable so shards keep authority during a blink, append-only fenced log so Raft replication is a later additive change not a rewrite). Write amplification from naive checkpointing is real — mitigated by tiered cadence (required, not optional).

phases.name: P8 — Ships: interior physics, dual-frame, boarding, ship transfers
phases.deliverables: A ship is its own shard (interior = private rapier3d world owned by the ship-shard throughout). Dual-frame: passengers are ChildOf(ShipId) sub-entities with authoritative frame ShipLocal(ship); you walk inside while the hull flies (Newtonian space physics on the exterior hull body). ReferenceFrameDef(rigid parent transform) lets the client composite interior pose THROUGH hull pose at one render tick. Boarding/disembark/EVA use the full seamless transfer machinery (the transition classes from P3, now with real interiors). Ship EXTERIOR authority transfers via the standard saga on the Ship(ShipId) key; the interior world is untouched (zero discontinuity for passengers). ATOMIC re-parent: directory bumps the ship key AND re-parents all ChildOf records in ONE redb transaction (kept within a single galaxy region so it never blocks future directory partitioning). External observers see ship+passengers as ONE versioned bundle (child-through-ship composed at a single consistent directory version — no passenger-teleport-relative-to-hull). SPIKE-10a (dual-frame interior physics) landed. ship_design redb table (ShipGrid as a voxel realm using the SAME shard-agnostic block code from P4/P6).
phases.definition_of_done: A player walks inside a ship interior while the ship flies under Newtonian physics; boards/disembarks/EVAs seamlessly (full machinery, kill -9 resilient); the ship warps/transfers exterior authority A->B with passengers feeling zero discontinuity and external observers seeing no passenger teleport. Ship interiors are voxel realms persisted per-ShipId (same block-edit durability as planets). MUST-NOT-REGRESS: every prior gate passes with ships in the mix.
phases.demo: A player builds/boards a ship, walks around inside while a second player flies it through space and lands near a planet; a third player on the planet surface watches the ship+passengers cross the planet-SOI boundary as one coherent bundle — all seamless, all kill -9 resilient.
phases.harness_scenarios: Dual-frame interior POSE-CONTINUITY under hull acceleration (staggered). Boarding/disembark/EVA seamless transfer (all classes with real interiors). Atomic N+1-key re-parent (ship+passengers in one txn, within one region). Versioned-bundle observer composition (no passenger teleport). Ship-warp exterior authority A->B with passengers. Concurrent-saga mutex (ship transferring while a passenger EVAs is serialized). Ship-interior block-edit durability. Full matrix re-run.
phases.risks: HIGHEST gameplay-complexity phase. Dual-frame physics is hard — mitigated by SPIKE-10a. The atomic re-parent is the one cross-key transaction that could block future directory partitioning — mitigated by keeping it within a single region (explicit scaling seam). Observer teleport is a subtle ordering bug — mitigated by the versioned bundle.

phases.name: P9 — Functional blocks + signal pipeline (shard-agnostic)
phases.deliverables: Functional blocks (lamps, switches, terminals, etc.) and the signal pipeline that wires them — RE-DERIVE from the old signal/ + config_state/grants design as SPEC. CRITICAL binding requirement: block/functional-block logic is SHARD-AGNOSTIC — the SAME code runs on any shard type (planet, ship, station). Functional-block config persisted in the per-realm config_state table; remote-access grants in the grants table (HMAC-signed per-channel, base64 key transfer for the tablet UI). Signals propagate within a realm; cross-realm signal forwarding rides the same fenced control-message machinery as block-edit forwarding. Client tablet/configurator UI (egui) for wiring blocks. config_state and grants survive crash via the same WAL/checkpoint discipline as block edits.
phases.definition_of_done: A player wires functional blocks (e.g., a switch toggling a lamp) on a planet AND inside a ship using the SAME code path; config persists across kill -9; grants allow another player remote access. The shard-agnostic property is proven by running the identical functional-block test fixture on a planet shard and a ship shard. MUST-NOT-REGRESS: full prior suite.
phases.demo: A player builds a wired control panel inside their ship (switches, lamps, a terminal) and the same kind of installation on a planet surface; both work identically and survive a crash. A second player is granted remote access to toggle a system.
phases.harness_scenarios: Functional-block signal propagation (deterministic). Shard-agnostic fixture (identical behavior planet vs ship). Config + grant durability across crash. Cross-realm signal forwarding (fenced, exactly-once). HMAC grant auth + revocation. Full matrix re-run.
phases.risks: The old signal pipeline used fire-and-forget tokio::spawn inside the tick — mitigated by re-expressing all broadcasts as outbound enqueues drained by the writer (bounded, back-pressured). Shard-agnostic-ness can erode if planet/ship paths diverge — mitigated by the identical-fixture test as a permanent gate.

phases.name: P10 — System/galaxy warp + on-demand destination provisioning
phases.deliverables: SystemWarp transition class (built LAST per all designs — needs on-demand dest-shard provisioning). AWAIT_PROVISION saga diversion -> PROVISION CHILD SAGA (keyed by provision_request_id, tied to TransferId) with durable de-provision compensation; dest self-registration GATED on 'am I still wanted for saga T?' (a pod that wins the schedule race after abort self-terminates — no zombie owner); idle-GC for unclaimed pods. Warp masking visual (system shrinks to a dot) covers provisioning latency while the UNDERLYING machinery stays seamless+robust. ProvisionProgress streamed to the client (warp visual stretches to eta). Source authority RETAINED until dest Committed (failed provisioning returns the player to a live source — never warp into nothing). Galaxy frame as integer light-year cells + f64 offset (f64 precision budget). brahe orbital mechanics for system layout. This exercises ALL the seamless machinery for the longest-latency, highest-uncertainty transition.
phases.definition_of_done: A player warps from one star system to another; the destination system shard is provisioned on demand; the player NEVER warps into nothing (failed/slow provisioning returns them to a live source); aborting mid-provision leaves no zombie shard. kill -9 the orchestrator during provisioning -> exactly one dest or clean abort-to-source. MUST-NOT-REGRESS: the ENTIRE accumulated suite (all transitions, terrain, physics, blocks, ships, signals) passes with warp added.
phases.demo: A player engages warp; the system shrinks to a dot (masking visual); a new system shard spins up on demand; they arrive seamlessly in a fresh procedurally-generated system — and if the operator kills the provisioner mid-warp, the player snaps safely back to the origin system. The full Star-Citizen-meets-Minecraft loop is now demonstrable end-to-end.
phases.harness_scenarios: Warp happy path (on-demand provision). Provision-timeout -> abort-to-source (player never stranded). Provision child-saga compensation (de-provision, self-registration-gating, no zombie). Orchestrator-crash-during-provision -> exactly-one-dest-or-clean-abort. Galaxy f64 precision (light-year-cell + offset). Full accumulated matrix re-run with warp.
phases.risks: On-demand provisioning is the highest-latency, most-failure-prone transition — mitigated by the child-saga-with-compensation, self-registration gating, and source-retained-until-commit (all four designs converge here). The bootstrap interest-set deadlock (no authoritative shard yet at a fresh destination) — mitigated by the stateless Spawn Resolver from P2.

phases.name: P11 — Combat + real-client feature-completion + scale-hardening
phases.deliverables: Combat (damage/destroy events on per-sub EVENTS streams, server-authoritative, no prediction). The real interactive client reaches feature parity with scripted clients across all transition classes (it has been growing in parallel since P1.5; here it fully replaces scripted clients for human play while scripted clients REMAIN the CI test drivers and load generators). Per-observer interest sets with add/remove diffs + ghost cap per observer (datagram budget). Cross-shard visibility via the same ghost/datagram machinery (two players on different shards see each other — no separate 1Hz digest). Connection-pool tuning (gateway<->shard small pool, 1/K HoL blast radius, redb off the send-path). Load test: N scripted clients in one Topology + a longer run_until, measuring datagram delivery, fsync p99, ghost staleness toward the thousands-of-players design target (dozens now).
phases.definition_of_done: Players fight (server-authoritative combat, damage/destroy delivered reliably per-sub without HoL-blocking other shards' events). The real client handles every transition class a human can trigger. Cross-shard players see each other smoothly. A load run of dozens of concurrent scripted clients holds all invariants and meets the latency/fsync/delivery budgets. MUST-NOT-REGRESS: the complete accumulated suite is the release gate.
phases.demo: A full multiplayer session: dozens of players across multiple planets, ships, and systems — building, flying, boarding, warping, and fighting — all seamless, all kill -9 resilient, all server-authoritative with no prediction. The complete Voxeldust vision, runnable on the k3d dev cluster.
phases.harness_scenarios: Combat damage/destroy delivery (reliable per-sub, no cross-shard HoL). Cross-shard mutual visibility (ghost stream). Per-observer interest add/remove diffs + ghost cap. Load test (N clients, budget assertions). EVENTS opened causally after SubscriptionOpened (X1, no overtake). Final full-suite release gate.
phases.risks: Scope-creep temptation to add gameplay features here without harness scenarios — mitigated by the standing rule that every feature lands with its must-not-regress scenarios. Scale beyond dozens is explicitly deferred (directory range-partition-by-RegionId is a designed-in seam, not built now).
